title: QCon San Francisco 2026: Scaling Tech by Aligning Humans
gist: At QCon San Francisco 2026, Netflix Principal Security Engineer Scott Behrens laid out a game-level playbook for staff-plus engineers to build a company-wide technical strategy (problem, pitch, tiger team, north star, bets, communication), drawn from Netflix's experience scaling internal AI agents. The article argues that aligning many teams around shared technical direction may become as valuable as the systems senior engineers build, especially as AI initiatives multiply.

insights.claim: At Netflix, multiple product strategies scaling internal AI agents began sharing similar technical risks, and without a common technical strategy underneath them teams were optimizing locally for different goals.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Parallel AI-agent initiatives inside large companies create shared, unmanaged technical risk — a demand signal for cross-team platform and governance tooling.
insights.locator: Behrens explained that the work started

insights.claim: Scott Behrens argues technical strategy can complement product strategy without waiting for it, and that lightweight strategies deliver faster than long technical documents.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Engineering orgs that wait for top-down product strategy before setting technical direction lose time; short strategy artifacts beat long design docs.
insights.locator: His view was that technical strategy

insights.claim: A strategy that brings people together can scale an engineer's impact further than any code that engineer could write alone, per Netflix's Scott Behrens.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Staff-plus leverage comes from alignment, not output — relevant to how firms value and structure senior engineering roles.

insights.claim: As organizations launch more initiatives in parallel, especially around AI, the ability of senior engineers to align many teams around a shared technical direction may become as valuable as the systems they build.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: AI initiative sprawl raises the premium on coordination capability; expect org-design and platform-consolidation efforts around AI.
insights.quote: the ability of senior engineers to align many teams around a shared technical direction may become as valuable as the systems they build

insights.claim: Behrens' playbook for finding a strategy-worthy problem mines company communications, incident trends, technical debt, conversations with other tech leads, and gaps between team charters, then tests whether the problem is worth solving now, foundational or compounding, and whether one is the right person to lead it.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: A reusable filter for prioritizing cross-cutting engineering problems; gaps between team charters are where systemic risk hides.
insights.locator: The talk presented a playbook organized

insights.claim: A strategy pitch should be a short problem statement covering intent, expected value, evidence-backed problems, why it matters now, and dated next steps, leaving approaches open and testing it early with colleagues including the likeliest dissenter.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Early exposure to dissent de-risks adoption of cross-team initiatives.

insights.claim: Behrens recommends a small tiger team focused on creating the strategy rather than executing it, mixing perspectives, comfortable with ambiguity, with manager support and an agreed scope, timeline and clear stop condition from the start.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Bounded strategy teams with explicit stop conditions avoid perpetual committees.
insights.locator: The presentation then covered building a small tiger team

insights.claim: Behrens' first strategy meeting at Netflix had far too many people yet still missed key functions; he says the most important trait of a good strategy team is making it safe to push back.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Team composition and psychological safety, not size, determine strategy quality.
insights.locator: He shared that his first meeting

insights.claim: A north star is a short aspirational statement that lets teams judge whether a piece of work moves the organization closer or farther from its goal; Behrens says writing a good one is harder than it looks and should be drafted with the team and paired with key outcomes that define what must be true.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: A clear north star does more steering than expected and is a cheap coordination mechanism across many teams.
insights.locator: With a team in place, the next step is a north star

insights.claim: Behrens defines strategy as simply a set of choices, written as bets of one choice versus another reasonable choice with the tradeoff named explicitly, kept short, few in number, and revisited over time.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Explicit tradeoff bets make strategy falsifiable and reviewable.
insights.locator: The strategy itself, according to Behrens

insights.claim: According to Behrens, if a strategy bet does not feel a little uncomfortable it is probably not a real bet.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Strategies with no uncomfortable tradeoffs signal no real prioritization.
insights.locator: The strategy itself, according to Behrens

insights.claim: Behrens advises expanding support for a technical strategy gradually from the immediate team to managers, directors and executives, recruiting champions across the organization and openly showing how feedback changed the strategy.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Visible incorporation of feedback is a lever for adoption of cross-org initiatives.
insights.locator: The talk also emphasized communication and feedback

insights.claim: Behrens' success test for a technical strategy is when he is not in the room and people can still explain the work.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: A practical measure of whether strategy has diffused beyond its author.
insights.quote: Success, he said, is when you are not in the room and people can still explain the work.
insights.locator: The talk also emphasized communication and feedback

insights.claim: Common failure modes of technical strategies are unclear problem statements, the wrong team, vague north stars, bets that are not really bets, and strategies that nobody knows exist.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Checklist for diagnosing stalled cross-team engineering programs.
insights.locator: He also reviewed common failure modes
